title: Present continuous: what's happening now
title_es: Presente continuo: lo que pasa ahora
goal: Decir en qué estás trabajando ahora mismo y distinguirlo del presente simple.

vocabulary.example: I'm testing the app right now.
She is working on the new design.
We are building a new feature.
I'm waiting for your answer.
We are working from home this week.

exercises.prompt: I am ___ on the login page right now. (work)
answers: working
exercises.explanation: Presente continuo = am / is / are + verbo con -ing. Se usa para acciones que están pasando en este momento: 'I am working'.

exercises.prompt: Shh! The team ___ a meeting.
exercises.explanation: Para algo que pasa ahora se necesitan las dos partes: el verbo to be (is) y el verbo con -ing (having). 'Having' solo, sin 'is', es incorrecto.

exercises.prompt: She usually ___ from home, but today she is at the office.
exercises.explanation: 'Usually' indica rutina → presente simple (works). El presente continuo es para lo que pasa ahora o es temporal.

exercises.prompt: Estoy esperando tu respuesta.
answers: I am waiting for your answer
I'm waiting for your answer
I am waiting for your reply
I'm waiting for your reply
I am waiting for your response
I'm waiting for your response
exercises.explanation: 'Esperar a alguien/algo' = 'wait FOR': 'I'm waiting for your answer'. Sin 'for' la frase queda incompleta.

exercises.answer: Are you working on the bug
exercises.explanation: Pregunta en presente continuo: Am / Is / Are + sujeto + verbo -ing. 'Are you working...?'.

exercises.prompt: I ___ what you mean.
exercises.explanation: Algunos verbos de estado (understand, know, want, like, need) casi nunca van en -ing, aunque hablemos de 'ahora': 'I understand', no 'I am understanding'.

title: Can, have to & should
title_es: Can, have to y should: habilidad, obligación y consejo
goal: Hablar de lo que sabes hacer, lo que tienes que hacer y dar consejos.

vocabulary.example: Communication is an important skill.
You have to attend the training.
Can you share your screen?
You should ask your manager.
Are you available tomorrow?

exercises.prompt: She ___ speak three languages.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' nunca cambia (no lleva -s) y va seguido del verbo base sin 'to': 'She can speak'.

exercises.prompt: ¿Puedes compartir tu pantalla?
answers: Can you share your screen
Could you share your screen
exercises.explanation: Peticiones: 'Can you...?' (normal) o 'Could you...?' (más cortés). Es una de las frases más usadas en videollamadas.

exercises.prompt: He ___ finish the report today. It's urgent.
exercises.explanation: 'Have to' sí cambia con he / she / it → 'has to'. Y 'must' nunca lleva 'to' ('must finish').

exercises.prompt: It's optional. You ___ come to the party.
exercises.explanation: 'Don't have to' = no es necesario. 'Mustn't' = está prohibido. Son muy diferentes aunque se parezcan.

exercises.prompt: You look tired. You ___ take a break. (consejo)
answers: should
exercises.explanation: 'Should' + verbo base sirve para dar consejos: 'You should take a break'. Igual que 'can', no lleva 'to' ni '-s'.
Negativo: can't (cannot) + verbo base. 'I can't attend the meeting' es la forma natural de avisar que no podrás ir.

vocabulary.example: This laptop is faster than my old one.
The basic plan is cheaper.
Python is better for this task.
It's the most popular tool.
The salary is higher in this job.

exercises.prompt: The new server is ___ than the old one. (fast)
answers: faster
exercises.explanation: Adjetivos cortos (una sílaba): + '-er' + than. fast → faster than, cheap → cheaper than.

exercises.prompt: This job is ___ than my current one.
exercises.explanation: Adjetivos largos (dos sílabas o más): 'more' + adjetivo + than. Nunca se combinan 'more' y '-er'.

exercises.prompt: Your English is ___ than last year!
exercises.explanation: Irregulares: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst. Hay que memorizarlos.

exercises.prompt: Es la herramienta más popular.
answers: It is the most popular tool
It's the most popular tool
exercises.explanation: Superlativo con adjetivo largo: 'the most' + adjetivo. Recuerda el sujeto 'It' (en inglés no se omite) y el orden: adjetivo antes del sustantivo.

exercises.prompt: Remote work is cheaper ___ commuting every day.
exercises.explanation: Para comparar se usa 'than' (que). Cuidado: 'then' significa 'entonces' y 'that' es 'ese/que' en otros contextos.

exercises.prompt: Friday is the ___ day of the week for me. (busy)
answers: busiest
exercises.explanation: Adjetivos que terminan en consonante + y: la 'y' cambia a 'i' → busy → busier → the busiest. Igual: easy → easiest.

title: There is / there are & prepositions
title_es: There is / there are y preposiciones de tiempo y lugar
goal: Describir dónde y cuándo pasan las cosas sin confundir in / on / at.

vocabulary.example: There is a problem with the server.
There are five people on the team.
We are in different time zones.
The office is on the third floor.
I don't work at the weekend.

exercises.prompt: ___ three new developers on our team.
exercises.explanation: 'Hay' se traduce como 'there is' (singular) o 'there are' (plural). Error típico: decir 'It has' o 'Has' por traducir 'hay' literalmente.

exercises.prompt: Hay un problema con la aplicación.
answers: There is a problem with the application
There's a problem with the application
There is a problem with the app
There's a problem with the app
There is an issue with the app
There's an issue with the app
There is an issue with the application
There's an issue with the application
exercises.explanation: 'Hay un problema' = 'There is a problem'. Y 'con' = 'with': 'a problem with the app'.

exercises.prompt: The call is ___ 3 p.m.
exercises.explanation: Regla de tiempo: AT + hora (at 3 p.m.), ON + día/fecha (on Monday), IN + mes/año/parte del día (in May, in the morning).

exercises.prompt: I started this job ___ 2023.
exercises.explanation: Con años y meses se usa 'in': in 2023, in March.

exercises.prompt: My laptop is ___ the desk. (sobre la superficie)
answers: on
exercises.explanation: 'On' = sobre una superficie (on the desk, on the wall). 'In' = dentro (in the box, in the room). 'At' = en un punto (at the door, at work).

exercises.prompt: ¿Cuál es la pregunta correcta?
exercises.explanation: En preguntas se invierte: 'Is there...?' / 'Are there...?'. 'Questions' es plural, así que 'Are there any questions?' — frase clásica al final de una presentación.
